subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Ravindra has left the friends' meeting saying that he __has bigger fish to catch to cook.__

options.text: he has bigger fish to fry
he has bigger beef to eat
he has big chicken to fry

solution:
The correct answer is: "**He has bigger fish to fry**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "**bigger fish to fry**" means that someone has more important or pressing matters to attend to. (किसी के पास ध्यान देने के लिए अधिक महत्वपूर्ण या अत्यावश्यक मामले हैं)
 
• The phrase is a common idiom in the English language.
 
 
• **Example**: *He had bigger fish to fry, so he didn't get involved in the minor office disputes.*
 
 

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

**Substituted sentence**: *Ravindra has left the friends' meeting saying that he has bigger fish to fry.*
